codeSystems.name: AdequacyInterpretationCS
codeSystems.title: Adequacy Interpretation
codeSystems.description: Per-nutrient and overall interpretations of a diet's nutrient levels against the applied requirement standard. The rules for `deficient` and `excess` are stated, proposed and pending ratification, on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

codeSystems.name: AnimalNutrientCS
codeSystems.title: Animal Nutrients (STUB)
codeSystems.description: STUB. Populate from the canonical nutrient list; map to SNOMED-vet / LOINC where possible. Ratio nutrients (e.g. Ca:P) need explicit handling, and non-linear ratios are excluded from the component model by design (see the [Animal Nutrient Adequacy Assessment](StructureDefinition-animal-nutrient-adequacy.html) profile). Which ratios count as non-linear is an open point on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

codeSystems.name: MaximumProvenanceCS
codeSystems.title: Maximum Provenance Codes
codeSystems.description: The kind of maximum a nutrient's range high is, which decides whether a value above it can be `excess`: only an authoritative maximum can. How the source template's maximum types map to these codes is stated, proposed and pending ratification, under Maximum types on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

codeSystems.name: NutrientDecileCS
codeSystems.title: Nutrient Decile Bands
codeSystems.description: The 14 bands of the Dynamic Decile System: four bands below the requirement minimum, as a share of the minimum, and ten deciles from the minimum to the range high. Where an entry gets a band, a value above the range high is in range-d10 unless it is below the minimum. The computation is stated, proposed and pending ratification, on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

codeSystems.name: RequirementStandardCS
codeSystems.title: Requirement Standards
codeSystems.description: Published nutrient requirement standards an adequacy check can be run against. Each standards body's code has a child code for each edition (is-a); record the edition's code when the edition is known. The editions are those the source template, Version 21OCT26b, cites.
